title: Route telemetry diary: odd regional routing behavior
content:
Quick personal log — not an ops runbook, just breadcrumbs while I'm poking at this.

Summary:
- Observed sporadic traffic steering from region-us-west -> region-eu-central for low-latency customers over ~2 hours (2026-02-11 02:10-04:30 UTC).
- Smart routing policy should prefer same-region unless load or health triggers fallback. In this case, source region seemed healthy by node metrics but control-plane decided to route out.
- Incident id: INC-2026-02-11-TEL-odd (ticket created, assigned to maya).

What I saw (timeline):
- 02:06 UTC: sudden increase in api-layer 5xx rate for a small shard (~3% -> 12%).
- 02:09 UTC: routing decision logs show aggregated health score for us-west fell below threshold for ~18 seconds.
- 02:10 UTC: control-plane issued route override, clients started hitting eu nodes.
- 02:28 UTC: us-west metrics recovered, but some sessions kept getting routed to eu for up to 25 minutes due to cached route decisions at edge.

Commands and checks I ran (notes + outputs copied where useful):
- quick curl to reproduce route header behavior:
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "X-Client-Region: us-west" -H "X-Trace-ID: t1-odd-0001" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"ping"}' -v
  -> response came from eu node: host: eu-infer-03.redwood.internal

- grabbed control-plane decision log around 02:09:
  grep "DECISION" /var/log/control-plane/route-decisions.log | sed -n '2026-02-11T02:08:30,2026-02-11T02:12:00p'
  sample line: 2026-02-11T02:09:17Z DECISION route=prefer-latency region=us-west score=0.42 health_agg=0.58 ttl=15s source=telemetry-agg-v2

- checked telemetry aggregator (telemetry-agg-v2) logs: some WARNs about delayed heartbeats from agent proxies (approx 60s gaps).
  kubectl logs telemetry-agg-v2 -n infra --since=30m | grep WARN | tail -n 20
  -> repeated: "WARN agent-heartbeat-mismatch agent=agent-proxy-17 last_seen=60s"

- edge cache (regional route cache) TTLs: config shows 60s default but ttl can be updated by control-plane decision. Observed TTL=15s in decision line above. That explains short window, but WHY did eu stick around 25m for some clients?

Hypotheses (raw):
1) Telemetry aggregator experienced intermittent ingestion delays -> produced lower health scores -> control-plane made a conservative route change.
   - root cause could be transient SQS backlog between agents -> aggregator (saw SQS metrics spike at 02:07).
2) Some clients (SDK, older routers) cache route decisions for longer than TTL due to a bug: fallback TTL not honored when route contains"preferred-region" attribute.
   - reproducer: older sdk builds (v0.9.x) will keep using sticky region header until reconnect. Check client versions in access logs.
3) KV-cache mismatch on the edge: route blacklisting state didn't get invalidated for all edge pods because of partitioned etcd write -> some pods still served eu routes.
   - check etcd leader logs and write latency.

Error snippets copied:
- api-layer logs (us-west): "upstream returned 502 after connecting to 10.11.9.27:5000, client=..."
- telemetry aggregator: "WARN agent-heartbeat-mismatch agent=agent-proxy-17 last_seen=60s"
- edge pod: "route-cache-miss fallback=eu-central forced_by=policy-guard"
- sdk logs (sample): "WARN route-cache TTL mismatch: cached_ttl=900s expected=15s"

Quick reproductions to run (next steps I left for myself):
- Force an explicit route-check from a test client and observe decision lifetime:
  1) make call with header X-Client-Region: us-west and X-Prefer: local, with trace id
  2) stream responses and verify X-Routed-Region header and X-Route-TTL header on every response
  curl -i -H "X-Client-Region: us-west" -H "X-Trace-ID: t1-repro-001" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ping

- Query datadog for agent ingestion latency:
  avg-last_5m:avg:telemetry.agent.ingest.latency{env:prod,region:us-west} by {agent} > 2000
  -> saw spikes matching 02:06-02:12 timeframe.

- Validate SDK version distribution for clients sending traffic during window:
  SELECT client_version, count(*) FROM access_logs WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-02-11T02:00' AND '2026-02-11T03:00' GROUP BY client_version

Immediate mitigations tried (results):
- forced a control-plane re-eval (POST /internal/v1/route-refresh) at 02:34 -> decisions recomputed and many edges updated. Noticed partial improvements but some clients still went to eu.
- rolled telemetry-agg-v2 to v2.0.1 (restart) at 02:45 -> heartbeats stabilized, no immediate repeat.

Follow-ups / TODOs: (assign)
- Maya: check SQS backlog metrics and any infra autoscaling events around 02:05-02:12 (priority) [CON-4321].
- Rafael: audit SDKs that respect route TTL, confirm whether v0.9.x has the caching bug. If so, draft hotfix or mitigation.
- Me (Evan): dig into edge route-cache invalidation paths, particularly etcd write visibility and watch latency. Look for partial partition during 02:07-02:15.

Notes / random thoughts:
- The control-plane uses telemetry-agg-v2's aggregated score and applies a hysteresis window (config: 10s down, 40s up). If aggregator emits noisy scores because of agent heartbeats, that could flip decisions quickly. Need to think about smoothing (moving median?) upstream to reduce oscillations.
- Also consider adding a per-client stickiness override: if a session pins to region, only route-change on severe degradation (>=50% error) or after session reconnect. Helps UX.
- We should add more trace headers in SDK responses (X-Route-Origin, X-Agg-Score) to make post-mortem easier.

Attachments I saved for this scratchpad:
- control-plane logs excerpt: /tmp/evan/route_decisions_02-09.log
- telemetry-agg logs: /tmp/evan/telemetry_02-06-02-10.log
- datadog queries captured in ticket CON-4321

If I come back to this later, checklist:
- [ ] repro with synthetic traffic (v0.9 vs v1.1 SDK)
- [ ] run etcd write-visibility test across edge pods
- [ ] tweak telemetry smoothing in a non-prod canary
- [ ] propose SDK patch to respect route TTL strictly

Random shorthand lines I typed while debugging (keep these, they helped):
- "agent backlog -> agg score dip -> control flip -> partial cache stale -> long tail eu hits"
- "TTL != cache_expiry in sdk -> sticky pops"
- "consider TTL enforcement at proxy edge (reject if cached longer than declared)"

End of scratchpad. Will dump findings into CON-4321 and update ticket once I validate SDK distribution.

-- Evan
